A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EA-L2D research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The substantial revision supports reliable comparison, although some dataset identities and reported settings require qualification.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulated-expert experiments, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–2 and multi-expertise and prior-information experiments in Figures 3–4.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark experiments and additional context-scaling, input-shift, latent-representation and loss-ablation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: V1 represents experts using posterior means and supplies four inputs to the rejector. V2 adds posterior variances, expands the rejector to six inputs, and replaces mean-only deferral-loss weighting with max(0, mean − alpha × standard deviation). These are substantive changes to the representation, network inputs and training objective (Section 4; Algorithm 1).

E1.justification: V2 removes CIFAR-10, GTSRB and Breast Ultrasound evaluations, adds Retinal OCT, and introduces HAM10000-to-BCN20000 input-shift testing. It also tests non-oracle expert populations with differing skill and uncertainty in Appendix F.4. The Axial Organ Slices and Liver Tumours settings share a citation and 11-class setup; the PDFs do not establish whether this represents renaming or changed underlying data.

E2.justification: The main Table 1 retains L2D-Pop, Pop-Avg and Multi-Expert L2D. However, the multi-expertise comparison expands: v1 Figure 3 compares only EA-L2D and L2D-Pop, whereas v2 Figure 3 also plots L2D-Avg and L2D-Multi, corresponding to Pop-Avg and Multi-Expert L2D, with the latter restricted to ID experts.

E3.justification: V1 trains on ID experts and evaluates separate ID/OOD groups. V2 Section 5.1 instead reports OOD performance on the ID group after training on the opposite group. The stated deferral-priority score changes from softmax-probability differences to logit differences. Reported settings also change, including Blood Cells context predictions from 40 to 120 and HAM10000 early-stopping patience from 100 to 50. The prior experiment changes from zero-context AURDAC evaluation to AURSAC versus context size.

E4.justification: V2 adds context-pool and sampled-context sensitivity studies, HAM10000-to-BCN20000 robustness testing, and an LCB ablation against mean-only, binary-specialty and classifier-only variants. Section 5.4 adds a t-SNE case analysis of L2D-Pop's OOD errors. The earlier prior experiment is expanded to investigate recovery from misspecified priors as context increases.

E5.justification: V1's main tables report mean and standard deviation across three seeds, with unspecified significance testing. V2 reports ten randomly sampled expert cohorts, explicitly specifies two-tailed paired t-tests, and adds ID/OOD significance markers. Its new ablation reports eight seeds with paired tests. Ten cohorts should not be interpreted as ten seeds or a documented increase in otherwise identical runs.

E6.justification: The main results are extensively replaced. For HAM10000 at p = 0.2, EA-L2D's ID/OOD AURSAC changes from 0.69 ± 0.03 and 0.87 ± 0.01 to 0.76 ± 0.08 and 0.75 ± 0.08. Changed methods and protocols prevent interpreting these as controlled gains or losses. V2 adds retinal, input-shift and ablation results, replaces the prior and multi-expertise curves, and removes v1's appendix table of 0–50% deferral-budget scores.

T1.justification: V1's convergence and expertise-identification propositions are consolidated into v2 Proposition 1. Substantive additions include a prior-misspecification recovery bound and proof, convergence of the LCB weight, and an asymptotic characterization of the modified loss and its deferral rule (Appendix C). Appendix A.2 also formalizes expert-agnosticism through explicit statistical-equivalence and class-permutation conditions.

C1.justification: The central contributions—expert-agnostic adaptation, reduced annotation requirements and prior integration—remain. V2 narrows the headline evaluation scope to medical imaging and replaces the 1–16% seen/4–28% unseen gains with up to 28% relative improvement on unseen experts and matching or exceeding seen-expert performance. It also explicitly promotes interpretability and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: V2 adds a hypothesis connecting L2D-Pop's latent-space structure to OOD errors and interprets uncertainty weighting as protection against misleading estimates from low-skill experts. Its limitations discussion emphasizes recovery from inaccurate priors and the potential coarseness of class-wise summaries, replacing v1's detailed clinician-calibration discussion. Appendix C explicitly distinguishes the learned asymptotic deferral rule from standard Bayes-optimal L2D deferral.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses computing hardware, Adam optimization, a six-layer rejector of width 256, and the Blood Cells classifier architecture. Appendix G adds dataset sizes, provenance, hosting platforms and licenses. Training hyperparameters are revised, while some earlier information, including weight-decay values and explicit context-batch sizes for the main experiments, is no longer supplied. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified implementation choices.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around constructed Bayesian statistics versus ANP-based latent representations, including Bayesian meta-learning, interpretability and computational complexity. It adds an agnostic-learning discussion citing MAML, TAML and Agnostic Federated Learning, plus extensive comparisons in Appendix A. V1's clinical self-calibration literature is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and methodology are extensively rewritten. Prior incorporation moves earlier within Section 4, experiments are organized around explicit research questions, and the appendices are reorganized around expanded discussion, pseudocode, proofs, experiments and dataset documentation. This goes beyond wording corrections or the insertion of new results.

P2.justification: The main document changes from two columns to one. Figures 1–2 are redrawn, Figure 3 expands into separate metric and expert-condition panels, and Figure 4 changes its axes and displayed experiment. V2 adds Figures 5–8, restructures Table 1 with a colored difference column and significance markers, removes v1's appendix Table 2, and adds distinct comparison-summary and ablation tables.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central generalization evidence: its reported design evaluates the same expert group under different training-expert conditions and uses ten cohorts with explicit paired tests, improving on v1's separate ID/OOD groups and three-seed summaries. Context scaling, prior recovery, input-shift testing and the uncertainty ablation provide more direct support for the claimed mechanisms. The asymptotic analysis also clarifies the boundary of Bayes optimality. These gains outweigh reduced benchmark and deferral-budget coverage, although inconsistent Liver Tumours dataset descriptions and omitted training details still limit reproducibility.
